subject: How the R / RPath / RFort references an entity's properties make to other scene objects are resolved after the instantiate pass.
headline: The deferred-reference list is an entity-command queue. Each record is one `"Command" { Command = E CommandType : <name> ; CommandTarget = R "<entity>" ; }` sub-block; 0046AAB0 matches the command name against the global command-type registry at 00E19A70, resolves the target name to an entity through 00925A90, and issues the order through 0077D600, which builds a " Mv" session message.

corrections.was: on a match it takes either the referenced object's position (+FCh/+100h/+104h) ...
corrections.is: the position on that branch is the OWNER's, EDI = record+0h loaded at 0046aad7; the matched registry object is the command and its position is never read
corrections.evidence: filtering the 0046aab0 listing for EDI shows one write, 0046aad7 MOV EDI,[EAX] with EAX = node+8h, and no reassignment before 0046ac03 MOV ECX,EDI

uncertainties: vtable[8] on a command object is read as 'requires an explicit target' from its effect here and its false default; no derived override was read.
The descriptor byte at +1h is 1 only on the position branch. 0077d600 copies the whole 16-bit word and tests byte 0 alone, so the meaning of byte +1h is provisional.
The descriptor float at +14h is always written 0.0 by this caller; what it means to 0077d600's callees was not established.
No run-time evidence: bsp_game.exe does not reach the scene instantiate pass, so the record counts above are static scans of the shipped .scn files, not observed queue lengths.
tooling_problems: bsp.py ghidra disasm --start rejects an address that is not an instruction boundary, which costs a retry when paging into the middle of a body; disasm-raw resyncs but desyncs on the first few instructions.
mcp__ghidra__search_byte_patterns ignores the mask argument: a masked pattern returns 'No matches found' while the same bytes matched exactly. Only exact patterns are usable.
A bare four-byte pattern search returns every hit in the image with no way to cap the output.
